summary: Concurrent worker reshard produced skewed per-key token consumption and transient quota rejections
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled worker reshard (automatic rescale), VerbatimSearch observed a spike of client-side retries and quota rejections for a subset of API keys. Rejections surfaced as 429-like behavior (quota_exhausted) despite overall tenant-level quota headroom.

Impact:
- ~12% of calls from VerbatimSearch saw immediate 429/quota_exhausted responses for 30-90s windows.
- ML feature extraction pipelines throttled, failing ~3k requests in peak interval.
- Customer-facing search latency increased as retry loops added backpressure.

Environment:
- Customer: VerbatimSearch LLC (dedicated pool)
- Region: prod - us-east (dedicated cluster id: ded-us-42)
- Models: redwood-mini-3b pinned v1.4
- Client: multiplexed HTTP uploader using 40 short-lived workers with exponential backoff

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start steady ingestion at ~110 rps with 40 concurrent upload workers.
2) Trigger an autoscale/resume event that causes reshard of worker threads (observed at 2026-03-12T02:14 UTC).
3) A subset of worker processes reconnect, receive new routing, and immediately send queued bursts to new frontends.
4) Token-bucket accounting at the per-key shard level recorded local exhaustion while tenant-level remaining quota was available.

Observed behavior:
- Burst of quota_exhausted rejections attributed to per-shard counters hitting local concurrency/token limits.
- Logs show many short-lived connections multiplexing requests to the same backend shard creating a hot-shard effect.
- Customer SDK retries (client-side) amplified the pressure for 40s until shard counters decayed.

Expected behavior:
- Resharding should preserve balanced per-key token distribution and avoid producing short windows of unilateral local exhaustion when tenant headroom exists.

Logs / Attachments:
- Prod request traces: trace-link: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces/ff22-reshard-20260312
- Quota dashboard snapshot: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/quotas/verbatim-reshard-20260312
comments: 2026-03-12 - Priya Raman (reporter): Customer reported sudden quota errors after automated scaling event. Provided error payloads and timestamps. Asked for priority triage.
2026-03-12 - Support -> SRE (Jordan McKee): Pinging quota and scheduler teams. Initial suspicion: local per-shard counters not rebalanced immediately during reshard. Attaching customer logs.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Jordan McKee): Observed per-shard token dips on cluster ded-us-42; tenant-level quota at ~78% free but 3/8 shards hit local exhaustion windows. Dumped counters to /var/tmp/reshard-dump-20260312.log and uploaded to ticket.

2026-03-13 - Scheduler eng (Maya Ortiz): Confirmed reshard produced uneven worker assignment due to hash ring churn combined with short TTL on per-key reservations. Proposed mitigation: short-term increase of per-key local token window and a fix to smooth transitions.

2026-03-14 - Support (Jordan McKee): Applied temporary mitigation for VerbatimSearch: increased per-key local bucket capacity from 50->150 tokens for 10 minutes, and advised client to slow initial reconnect burst. Monitoring continues.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
1) Global quota bug (unlikely): tenant-level quota showed plenty of headroom.
2) Per-shard accounting race during reshard: supported by counter dumps where three shards recorded near-zero local tokens while others had surplus.
3) Client-side retry amplification: SDK created short back-to-back requests on reconnect causing burst.

Key findings:
- Timeline alignment: reshard event at 2026-03-12T02:14 UTC matches first spike in rejections.
- Counter dump: per-shard token_count for customer keys: [shard-3: 2, shard-5: 0, shard-7: 4, others: >200].
- Router logs show reconnections from 15 distinct workers concentrated on shard-5 within 12s window.
- No evidence of model-serving overload (GPU metrics stable).

Temporary detection rule added to quota-service: if local shard token drops below 10% while tenant headroom >30%, emit a 'hot-shard' alert and auto-apply a transient local-cap increase up to 3x for 60s. Link to incident timeline: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-20260312-reshard
resolution:
Mitigation performed and next steps:
- Short-term: increased per-key local bucket limits for VerbatimSearch for 10 minutes during the incident window; coordinated with customer to stagger reconnect attempts. Customer confirmed error rate reduced to baseline.
- Medium-term: scheduler patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1784) implemented smoothing on reshard handoff to avoid directing bursts to a single shard. The patch introduces a handoff grace period and gradual reassignment of active connections.
- Long-term: quota-service change to detect hot-shard conditions and temporarily redistribute local tokens or forward requests to sibling shards rather than rejecting. Follow-up work: INT ticket created to formalize QA and rollout plan (INT-4112).

Follow-up items assigned:
- SRE: finalize hot-shard detection tuning and runbook (owner: Jordan McKee).
- Scheduler: roll out smoothing patch to prod canary and monitor for regressions (owner: Maya Ortiz).
- Support/Account: coordinate with VerbatimSearch on SDK backoff recommendations and update docs with best practices for reconnect behavior (owner: Priya Raman).

Status: Mitigation successful; code changes in review and in canary. Customer impact resolved; ticket remains open until scheduler/safety patches are in prod and runbook published.
